rationale_evidence.anchor: one aggregate with two parts, or two aggregates sharing an identity? ... I-4 is itself a spanning invariant — a negative one.
rationale_evidence.statement: Facing evidence that no positive invariant spans the lifecycle and authority parts of the record (an honest finding that argues for splitting), the proposal nonetheless keeps one root because I-4 (they must never merge) is a negative spanning invariant needing a single holder that can see both parts, and the write boundary is one file.

rationale_evidence.anchor: (D) invariant violation — NO ... (D), and the defect is in the proposal's I-5 row, not in the invariant, the mechanism, or the model.
rationale_evidence.statement: C-3's classification is independently derived (before reading the refinement's own reasoning) as (D): the observed non-Governance recorder on a HANDOFF transition is not an invariant violation, missing enforcement, or a missing conceptual distinction, but simply a table cell in the proposal that measured I-5 (an authority-part invariant) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids conflating.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Verdict: (D) — a mis-scoped invariant statement. ... D.1 — The observation and the invariant live in different parts of the aggregate.
rationale_evidence.statement: Independent classification (derived from evidence E-1..E-8 before considering any candidate) concludes (D): the observed `architecture`-recorded HANDOFF is not a violation, missing enforcement, or missing distinction, but a case of measuring an authority-part invariant (I-5) against a lifecycle-part transition, which I-4 itself forbids; both instances were also the mechanism's required actor (DP-3), and a HANDOFF confers no ownership regardless.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 'Consistency is determined by invariant ownership, not by event-driven communication.' ... EKS: No event bus. Yet: 11/11 workflow invariants → single identifiable owner → executable tests ... SUPPORTED: non-distributed systems / UNKNOWN: distributed KnowledgeOS
rationale_evidence.statement: DeepSeek tests and finds current consistency is achieved through invariant ownership, not event-driven integration: EKS has no event bus yet 11/11 workflow invariants have a single identifiable owner with executable tests; PKS has no event architecture yet governance invariants define ownership; AIP has no event-driven architecture yet BC-7 mechanically owns orchestration invariants. Explicitly does NOT over-generalize: classified SUPPORTED for non-distributed systems, UNKNOWN for a distributed KnowledgeOS.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 11 of 11 workflow-record invariants have a single, identifiable owner and an executable test. Every invariant outside the workflow record either has no owner or has an advisory-only owner.
rationale_evidence.statement: Invariant-ownership table finding: all 11 workflow-record invariants (Inv A-J, G-2/G-3, R8) have a single identifiable code owner and an executable test (mostly class A); by contrast grant-identity uniqueness, temporal ordering of authority, and process/actor authenticity have NO owner at all (class E), while corpus reference integrity, identifier uniqueness, document schema conformance, and placement correctness have only advisory-only owners (class C) -- 'every invariant outside the workflow record either has no owner or has an advisory-only owner.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: Every invariant BC-7 (the workflow engine) owns is mechanically enforced; almost every invariant outside BC-7 is declared only
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline structural finding -- the invariant asymmetry: assurance is strong where it is executable (BC-7) and weak where it is prose (outside BC-7). 'The platform mechanically protects orchestration, and protects knowledge/verification/communication only by declaration.' Stated as the single most important structural property of AIP's current architecture.

Seven headline findings: (1) AIP is a registry-first, session-based engineering operating platform, not a product domain; (2) the implemented core is the workflow/authority engine plus guard surfaces, with knowledge/review components deferred/not built and verification under construction; (3) the invariant asymmetry is the load-bearing structural property; (4) the authority record lives in an ignored runtime directory (the durability inversion), decided-but-not-executed; (5) the D1/D2 decision state is contradictory across the corpus, surfaced not reconciled; (6) four unowned capabilities form one control loop with C-10/C-14 existence UNDECIDED; (7) AIP self-records four capability failures (EKS-01..04) -- the platform observing its own uneven assurance.
